$comment: Scoop manifest template. The release workflow substitutes 0.5.27,
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.27/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip and 16a17ba82412eb6b28562e08f5ac374f3586656ccb042fe2aee56e7d296a5e0d and commits the result to the bucket repository.
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.27/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip is on the public downloads CDN, never a GitHub release: this
repository is private, so a GitHub URL is a 404 for everyone who would
install from a public bucket. There is no `checkver`/`autoupdate` for the
same reason: the release workflow pushes the new manifest itself, and
the GitHub API it would poll is not open to the public either.
16a17ba82412eb6b28562e08f5ac374f3586656ccb042fe2aee56e7d296a5e0d is read from the .sha256 the release publishes beside the
archive, the same one the patched PowerShell installer verifies against,
so there is exactly one published hash per archive.
post_install: Write-Host 'yoink installed. Run `yoink doctor` to check it over.'
